title: S3GA: Towards Scalable Self-Supervised Learning for Large Scale Graph Alignment

problem.claim: Graph alignment is an NP-hard combinatorial challenge.

gap.claim: Existing graph alignment methods generally target small-scale graphs because computational complexity grows quadratically with the number of nodes, while large real-world graphs often lack sufficient alignment labels.

contributions.claim: A self-supervised learning framework for graph alignment on million-node graphs without alignment labels.
An Alignment-Aware Clustering method that jointly partitions source and target nodes to keep likely aligned pairs within the same cluster.
A Topology-Aware Repartition method that uses pseudo-alignment labels as anchors for re-clustering while preserving detailed structural information within clusters.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their self-supervised learning framework as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments greatly reduce computational demands and maintain high alignment accuracies in large-scale graph applications.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph alignment is computationally difficult, and existing methods are limited by scale and label scarcity.
Recent techniques use alignment labels to divide large source and target graphs into smaller graphs for separate alignment.
S3GA uses a divide-and-conquer framework with joint alignment-aware clustering, topology-aware repartitioning, and self-supervised graph representation learning.
The authors report improved computational demands and high alignment accuracies in large-scale applications.

source_observation.claim: The method jointly partitions source and target nodes and uses pseudo-alignment labels to guide repartitioning.

interpretation.claim: When explicit alignment labels are scarce, jointly structuring both sides and iteratively using pseudo-labels may preserve cross-graph correspondence and local topology.

application.claim: Large-scale alignment systems may benefit from combining divide-and-conquer decomposition with correspondence-aware partition refinement.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy remains effective when pseudo-alignment labels are noisy or when graph structures differ substantially.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, and quantitative results are not specified.
Runtime, memory usage, scalability limits, and pseudo-label quality are not specified.
The abstract does not describe failure cases or sensitivity to graph heterogeneity.
